review_note: Independent review of the m26 re-record. The oracle is a dense base-R joint Laplace over the mu and sigma random effects (nlminb mode, gradient below 1e-8, positive-definite Hessian, 1e-4 on logLik), with no package helper. Case (a), the q2 block with sd(id, coef='x') ~ w plus a sigma (1|g) SD, has built-in sensitivity: a misaligned slope SD and a flipped rho each move the oracle by more than 1. Cases (b) and (c1) cover the iid mu-intercept and sigma-intercept rows. Case (b) had no in-test perturbation, so I ran one on Totoro without editing files. At the fit, the oracle equals logLik to 4 decimals (-708.8206). Swapping the mu and sigma SD vectors moves it by 0.51, about 5000 times the 1e-4 tolerance. Reversing the mu SDs moves it by 17.8. The third row (mu:x1 of the iid correlated block) is exercised by case (a). Its intercept-SD member is constant there and is not claimed. All 4 manifest files rehash with 0 mismatches, and the rerun shows 30 expectations, 0 failures, 0 skips. This does NOT establish the mu:I member of the q2 block, sigma-endpoint q2 blocks, crossed or nested sigma rows, interval calibration or coverage, or Julia parity. The swap sensitivity for (b) was shown in a scratch run, not in the test, and is evaluated at fitted parameters only.
